title: Label customers by spending
prompt: For every customer, return first_name, spent and tier. spent is the total of quantity * unit_price over the items of the customer's orders, leaving out cancelled orders, and 0 for a customer with no such orders. tier is gold when spent is 5000 or more, silver when it is 1000 or more, and bronze otherwise. Put the highest spent first, and sort customers with the same spent by first_name.
hints: The report has one row per customer. Which table must the main query start from?
Work out spent per customer_id in a step. LEFT JOIN it to customers and turn a missing total into 0.
CASE WHEN spent >= 5000 THEN 'gold' WHEN spent >= 1000 THEN 'silver' ELSE 'bronze' END, with the larger limit tested first

wrongAnswers.misconception: Uses an inner join, which leaves out customers who have spent nothing.
Tests the lower limit first, so nobody is ever gold.

feedback: Check three customers: the biggest spender, one who has never ordered, and one whose only orders were cancelled.
